info.name: remote_control_backend
info.description:
Manual end-to-end testing of remote_control_backend.

The contract this collection follows is docs/ENDPOINTS.md. If a request here
ever disagrees with that file, the file wins and the collection is the one to
fix.

## Before starting

1. Run the backend (`npm run start:dev`).
2. Create the first administrator with `npm run bootstrap:admin`.
3. Import the environment `remote_control_backend.postman_environment.json`
   and select it.
4. Set `baseUrl`, `userEmail` and `userPassword` there. No password is stored
   in this collection.

## End-to-end flow

```text
01  Login user                              (01 - Authentication)
02  Create device                           (02 - Devices)
03  Generate enrollment                     (02 - Devices)
04  Activate device                         (03 - Device enrollment ...)
05  Device login                            (03 - Device enrollment ...)
06  Device check-status                     (03 - Device enrollment ...)
07  Create support request                  (04 - Support requests - Device)
08  List support requests (status=WAITING)  (05 - Support requests - Technician)
09  Assign support request                  (05 - Support requests - Technician)
10  Accept support request                  (04 - Support requests - Device)
11  Create remote session                   (06 - Remote sessions)
12  Get current remote session - Device     (06 - Remote sessions)
13  Close remote session                    (06 - Remote sessions)
```

Step 09 requires the device to be ONLINE, and step 11 depends on step 09. A
device is ONLINE only while it holds an open Socket.IO connection to the
/devices namespace, which no HTTP request can create: without the Flutter app
(or another Socket.IO client) connected with the Device JWT, "Assign support
request" answers 409 and the flow stops there.

## Realtime

The two Socket.IO namespaces

```text
/devices
/technicians
```

are documented in docs/REALTIME.md. They are not representable as HTTP requests
and are deliberately absent from this collection — there are no fake REST calls
for presence, signaling or WebRTC here.

## Authentication

Nothing is inherited: every request carries its own Authorization header, either
`Bearer {{userToken}}` (technician/admin) or `Bearer {{deviceToken}}` (tablet).
The two token types are signed with different secrets and are never
interchangeable.

item.name: 01 - Authentication
item.description:
Technician/user identity (User JWT). See docs/ENDPOINTS.md — "Authentication — Web".

Run "Login user" first: every request in folders 02, 05 and 06 needs the
{{userToken}} it stores.

exec: pm.test('Response carries a user token', function () {
pm.test('Response carries the user id', function () {

request.description:
Step 01 of the end-to-end flow.

Public endpoint. Answers 200 (not 201): logging in does not create a resource.

Fill {{userEmail}} and {{userPassword}} in the environment with the administrator
created by `npm run bootstrap:admin`. No password is stored in this collection.

Stores: userToken.

exec: pm.test('Response carries a renewed user token', function () {
pm.test('Response carries the user id', function () {

request.description:
Validates the current User JWT and returns the user with a renewed token.
The stored {{userToken}} is replaced with the renewed one.

Stores: userToken.

exec: pm.test('The created account is active', function () {
pm.test('The password is never returned', function () {
pm.test('The created user has an id', function () {

request.description:
Administrative user creation. Requires an admin token: a `tecnico` gets 403.

The `token` in the response belongs to the CREATED user, not to the admin who
made the call, so this request deliberately does not overwrite {{userToken}}.

The password in the body is a throwaway example value for local testing.

item.name: 02 - Devices
item.description:
Administrative device management. User JWT with role admin or tecnico.
The tablet never calls these routes.

exec: pm.test('Response carries the device id', function () {
pm.test('Response carries the public id', function () {
pm.test('A new device is enabled and offline', function () {

request.description:
Step 02 of the end-to-end flow.

All fields are optional; an empty body {} is accepted. The backend generates
id and publicId. The device is created with no credential: it cannot
authenticate until it is enrolled.

Stores: deviceId, publicId.

exec: pm.test('The response is an array', function () {

request.description: All devices, newest first. Each row carries its realtime isOnline.

exec: pm.test('It is the requested device', function () {

request.description: One device by its UUID. A non-UUID id returns 400 before the handler runs.

Updates the administrative fields of a device. Only the properties present in
the body are applied. id, publicId, createdAt and updatedAt are rejected.

This body only renames the device on purpose. Sending "isActive": false also
force-closes every open Socket.IO connection of the device and makes all its
REST calls fail with 401, which would interrupt the end-to-end flow.

exec: pm.test('Response carries the enrollment code', function () {
pm.test('Response carries the device id', function () {
pm.test('Response carries the public id', function () {

request.description:
Step 03 of the end-to-end flow.

Generates the 6-digit activation code the technician reads out to the user of
the tablet. Issuing a new code revokes every previous pending code of that
device. The code travels in clear text once, in this response only; it expires
in 30 minutes and is single-use.

Stores: enrollmentCode, deviceId, publicId.

item.name: 03 - Device enrollment and authentication
item.description:
The tablet identity. Activation is public (the enrollment code is what
authorises it) and everything afterwards uses the Device JWT, which is signed
with a different secret than the user one and is never interchangeable with it.

exec: pm.test('Response carries the device secret', function () {
pm.test('Response carries the device id', function () {
pm.test('Response carries the public id', function () {

request.description:
Step 04 of the end-to-end flow.

Public endpoint. Exchanges publicId + code for the permanent deviceSecret,
which is delivered once and only here. Every rejection reason answers the same
401 on purpose.

Stores: deviceSecret, deviceId, publicId.

Security note: deviceSecret is written to the Postman environment because this
collection is a local testing tool. It is never logged to the console.

exec: pm.test('Response carries a device token', function () {

request.description:
Step 05 of the end-to-end flow.

Exchanges the permanent deviceSecret for a Device JWT (24h by default).
publicId is not accepted here: it does not authenticate. Answers 200.

Stores: deviceToken.

exec: pm.test('It is the authenticated device', function () {
pm.test('No token is renewed here', function () {

request.description:
Step 06 of the end-to-end flow.

Validates the current Device JWT. Unlike GET /auth/check-status it does NOT
renew the token; renewal is done through POST /device-auth/login.

item.name: 04 - Support requests - Device
item.description:
Device JWT. The device identity always comes from the token: no endpoint in
this group accepts a deviceId.

Accept, Reject and Cancel are alternative outcomes, not consecutive steps. The
main flow uses Accept.

exec: pm.test('Response carries the support request id', function () {

request.description:
Step 07 of the end-to-end flow.

The user of the tablet presses "request assistance". Empty body. A device may
have only one active request (WAITING, ASSIGNED, ACCEPTED) at a time; a second
one answers 409.

Stores: supportRequestId.

exec: pm.test('The response carries the supportRequest field', function () {
pm.test('The active request has an id', function () {

request.description:
How the tablet recovers state after a restart, a reconnection or a missed
Socket.IO event. Having no active request is normal and answers 200 with
{ "supportRequest": null }, not 404.

Stores: supportRequestId, when there is an active request.

Step 10 of the end-to-end flow.

The user authorises the assigned technician: ASSIGNED -> ACCEPTED. Empty body.
ACCEPTED does not create a remote session; the technician still has to call
POST /remote-sessions.

Alternative to Accept: the user refuses the assigned technician.
ASSIGNED -> REJECTED, terminal. Only valid from ASSIGNED; anything else is 409.

The user withdraws the request. Allowed from WAITING, ASSIGNED and ACCEPTED.

Once a live RemoteSession exists, cancelling is refused with 409: the tablet
must close the session with POST /device/remote-sessions/:id/close instead.

item.name: 05 - Support requests - Technician
item.description: User JWT with role admin or tecnico. Reading the queue is not ownership-scoped.

exec: pm.test('The response is an array', function () {

request.description:
Step 08 of the end-to-end flow.

The queue, oldest first, with the device and its realtime isOnline. Remove the
status query parameter to get every request; an unknown value is a 400, not an
empty list.

exec: pm.test('It is the requested support request', function () {

request.description: One support request by id. Any admin/tecnico can read any request.

exec: pm.test('The technician comes from the token', function () {

request.description:
Step 09 of the end-to-end flow.

The technician takes the request: WAITING -> ASSIGNED. Empty body on purpose —
technicianId is not accepted, the technician is the authenticated user.

Requires the device to be ONLINE (connected to the /devices Socket.IO
namespace); an offline device answers 409 and the request stays WAITING.

item.name: 06 - Remote sessions
item.description:
The technician routes are mounted under /remote-sessions (User JWT) and the
device ones under /device/remote-sessions (Device JWT).

Every technician route is ownership-scoped: the session must belong to the
authenticated technician. Being admin is not an exemption — it answers 404 like
anybody else, and /remote-sessions/current answers remoteSession null.

The two close requests are alternatives: whoever closes first wins and the
other side gets 409. Each close notifies the other end over Socket.IO.

exec: pm.test('Response carries the remote session id', function () {

request.description:
Step 11 of the end-to-end flow.

Only an ACCEPTED request assigned to this technician authorises remote control.
supportRequestId is the only accepted field: sending deviceId or technicianId
fails with 400.

Stores: remoteSessionId.

exec: pm.test('The response carries the remoteSession field', function () {
pm.test('The live session belongs to the authenticated technician', function () {
pm.test('A current session is never CLOSED', function () {

request.description:
Step 12b of the end-to-end flow.

The live session of the authenticated technician, or
{ "remoteSession": null }. "Live" means CONNECTING or ACTIVE; a CLOSED session
is never returned here, and having none is 200, not 404.

This is how remote_control_web recovers after an F5 without trusting a
remoteSessionId kept in the browser, and what it re-reads when it receives
remote-session:closed on the /technicians namespace.

Ownership comes from {{userToken}} only: technicianId is not accepted anywhere,
and an admin recovers their own sessions, not somebody else's.

Stores: remoteSessionId, when there is a live session.

exec: pm.test('It is the requested session', function () {

request.description:
The session by id, closed ones included. Use it to read one specific session,
for example the one named by a remote-session:closed event. To recover "the
session I have open right now", use Get current remote session - Technician.

exec: pm.test('The response carries the remoteSession field', function () {
pm.test('The live session has an id', function () {

request.description:
Step 12a of the end-to-end flow.

The live session of the authenticated device, or { "remoteSession": null }.
"Live" means CONNECTING or ACTIVE; a CLOSED session is never returned here.

Stores: remoteSessionId, when there is a live session.

exec: pm.test('The session is closed by the technician', function () {

request.description:
Step 13 of the end-to-end flow.

The technician ends the assistance: the session becomes CLOSED with
endedBy TECHNICIAN and its support request becomes COMPLETED in the same
transaction. Emits remote-session:closed to the device.

exec: pm.test('The session is closed by the device', function () {

request.description:
Alternative to closing as the technician: the user of the tablet ends the
assistance. CLOSED with endedBy DEVICE, and the support request becomes
COMPLETED in the same transaction.

Emits remote-session:closed to the owning technician on /technicians, after the
transaction commits. The web app answers that event with
GET /remote-sessions/current.
